svg.aria-label: Diagram: why Cloud Router is a control plane that speaks BGP and does no packet forwarding, since Andromeda handles all routing and forwarding; the two kinds of learned route, with custom learned routes simulating a peer you do not control and withdrawing automatically when the session drops, unlike a static route; the two best path selection modes where legacy is both the default and the recommendation despite ignoring AS path across BGP tasks, and standard follows RFC 4271 and enables AS path prepending; the tie-break ladder of shortest AS path then origin type then smallest MED; the two-level advertisement model where a BGP session set to custom overrides the router entirely; and the dynamic route quota that drops whole destinations deterministically and records them in a Cloud Logging event
svg.title: Cloud Router and BGP: a control plane that forwards nothing, where the default best-path mode ignores AS path
svg.text: Cloud Router does not route. It speaks BGP and installs routes; Andromeda forwards packets.
And the default best-path mode ignores the attribute every BGP engineer reaches for first.
The name is the trap
CLOUD ROUTERS DO NOT PROVIDE PACKET ROUTING OR FORWARDING CAPABILITY. Andromeda handles
all of that; Cloud Router manages the corresponding BGP sessions.
So it has no throughput, no bandwidth and no datapath to size. It is a BGP speaker and
responder that creates DYNAMIC ROUTES in the VPC network.
Cloud NAT uses it for the control plane only — no BGP session management at all.
Two kinds of learned route, and why the custom one beats a static route
BGP RECEIVED: from an on-premises router, another Cloud Router, a Router appliance VM, or
another cloud provider’s router.
CUSTOM LEARNED: configured by hand to SIMULATE a peer, for when you do not control the
remote router. Its priority is treated like a MED value.
The reason to prefer it over a static route: a custom learned route is AUTOMATICALLY
WITHDRAWN when the BGP session for its next hop goes down. A static route is not.
Two best-path modes — and Google recommends the one that ignores AS path
LEGACY is the DEFAULT for a new VPC network, and the RECOMMENDED mode unless you need
something from standard mode.
But in legacy mode AS path is relevant only WITHIN a single BGP task — the dynamic route
control plane does not use it at all. Google says: do not rely on AS-path length when
different Cloud Router tasks are involved for the same prefix.
STANDARD mode follows RFC 4271, considers AS path across all Cloud Routers in the VPC, and
is what makes AS PATH PREPENDING work. The flexible mode is the one not recommended.
The tie-break ladder inside one BGP task
1. SHORTEST AS PATH length. 2. ORIGIN TYPE: IGP beats EGP, EGP beats Incomplete.
3. SMALLEST MED. In global dynamic routing mode an INTER-REGIONAL COST is added to the MED
of routes arriving from other regions, which is how region affinity is expressed.
And across the whole VPC: DYNAMIC ROUTES ALWAYS RANK BELOW STATIC ROUTES.
Advertisement is set at two levels, and the session wins
Mode is configurable on the ROUTER and on each BGP SESSION. A session left on default
inherits the router’s configuration, whichever that is.
A session set to CUSTOM DOES NOT INHERIT the router’s configuration at all — so one
session can silently diverge from every other session on the same router.
Three sharp edges
QUOTA: over the dynamic-route limit, the control plane DROPS ALL ROUTE INFORMATION for whole
destinations that sort beyond it. Find them in route_quota_events in Cloud Logging.
IPv6: no IPv6 BGP for Classic VPN, Router appliance, or Cross-Cloud Interconnect attachments.
EXTERNAL IPv6 subnet ranges are NEVER advertised by subnet advertisement — only as custom.
